item.title: Tokyo Station & Marunouchi — Guide
item.description: Tokyo Station’s Marunouchi side is one of the city’s most striking architectural sights: a magnificent red-brick Renaissance-style building originally opened in 1914 and beautifully restored to its original form, with elegant domes and a stately facade that lights up handsomely at night. Far more than a place to catch a train, the station is a vast destination in itself, with an enormous underground world of shopping streets and restaurants — including ‘Tokyo Character Street’ (with shops for popular anime and TV characters), ‘Tokyo Ramen Street’ (gathering famous ramen shops), sweets streets and countless eateries.

item.title: Imperial Palace Guide: East Gardens, Edo Castle Ruins & Tokyo's Green Heart
item.description: In the very centre of Tokyo, surrounded by the glass towers of Marunouchi and the rush of the financial district, lies a vast island of moats, stone walls, pine forests, and manicured gardens: the Tokyo Imperial Palace, official residence of the Emperor of Japan. This is the site of Edo Castle, once the largest fortress in the world and the seat of the Tokugawa shoguns who ruled Japan for 260 years.
